cases.title: Stock Income
cases.name: Nancy & Paul Pelosi
cases.summary: Nancy Pelosi's 2025 annual disclosure reports more than $7 million in income from three spouse-owned stock positions: Apple, Amazon and Nvidia. The filing puts the family's financial interest in major technology companies on the record while she served in Congress.

findings.text: Apple: over $5 million in capital gains and dividends. Amazon: $1,000,001–$5 million in capital gains. Nvidia: $1,000,001–$5 million in capital gains and dividends. These are income brackets, separate from the value of the stock holdings.

The more-than-$7-million headline is a conservative lower-bound calculation from three nonoverlapping income rows. It is not an estimate of total household income, net worth growth, or gains caused by political influence.

The same report lists spouse salary from Financial Leasing Services and management-fee sources without publishing dollar amounts. These are additional disclosed business connections, not amounts included in the stock-income subtotal.

money.label: Apple stock income
money.cash_counterparty: Not fully identified: capital gains reflect securities transactions, not necessarily payments by Apple

money.label: Nvidia stock income
money.cash_counterparty: Not fully identified: capital gains reflect securities transactions, not necessarily payments by Nvidia

calculation.deduplication: Three distinct Schedule A common-stock income rows; exclude option asset values, sale proceeds and charitable transfers. Do not add this subtotal to its component rows.

cases.accountability: What safeguards separate a sitting lawmaker's policy responsibilities from a household portfolio producing multimillion-dollar income? The financial overlap is documented; a claim that privileged information caused these gains requires separate evidence.

response.text: Pelosi told CNN that her husband makes the investments and denied insider trading. She publicly supported a congressional stock-trading ban in July 2025.

cases.what_is_established: Large spouse investment income during congressional service and named corporate holdings.
cases.what_is_not_established: Political causation, insider trading, exact net after-tax profit, or that the issuers transferred the entire reported gains to the family.
next_evidence: Match all relevant PTR sale lots to acquisition disclosures to test holding periods and avoid confusing gross proceeds with gains.
Build a dated legislative/committee-action timeline only where a specific policy overlap exists; compare against sector returns and ordinary diversification explanations.
Keep unquantified spouse business income visible as a named connection without treating it as zero.

cases.title: Foreign Payments
cases.name: Henry & Imelda Cuellar

people.name: Henry Cuellar
people.role: U.S. representative, Texas, during the prosecution and pardon

people.name: Imelda Cuellar
people.role: Spouse; alleged recipient through controlled companies

headline.label: Alleged foreign payments
headline.recipient: Imelda-controlled companies, allegedly for the couple's benefit

cases.summary: Federal prosecutors accused Henry and Imelda Cuellar of receiving roughly $600,000 through arrangements involving an Azerbaijani state-owned energy company and a Mexican bank. The indictment described payments routed through the wife's companies in exchange for official favors. Both denied wrongdoing and received presidential pardons before trial.

findings.text: The May 2024 indictment alleged sham consulting payments from December 2014 through November 2021. Those payment dates fall outside this site's four-year financial window.
The Texas Tribune identified the bank as Banco Azteca and reported guilty pleas by two political consultants involved in the alleged payment route. Their pleas do not establish the Cuellars' guilt.
The signed warrant grants Henry and Imelda a full and unconditional pardon dated December 2, 2025. The case did not produce a trial verdict against them.

money.label: Alleged foreign-source payments
money.legal_recipient: Imelda Cuellar-controlled companies, according to prosecutors
money.personal_allocation: Alleged household benefit; exact split between Henry, Imelda, companies and intermediaries not established here

cases.accountability: The alleged route links foreign commercial interests, a lawmaker's official actions and companies controlled by his spouse. The pardon ended the prospect of a trial verdict; it did not supply a public accounting of the payments. That makes the underlying financial trail a concrete reporting question, not a blank profile.

response.text: Henry and Imelda Cuellar denied wrongdoing. President Trump pardoned both before trial. Present the payments as allegations, not convictions.

cases.what_is_established: The indictment, its named payment mechanism and historical period, related consultant pleas, and the pardon.
cases.what_is_not_established: A verdict that the Cuellars took bribes, a new FY2023–FY2026 payment total, or an exact personal-profit allocation.
next_evidence: Extract each indictment payment and intermediary from exhibits, with bank/deposit date and recipient legal entity; avoid counting the same routed dollar more than once.
Match consultant plea admissions against the Cuellar allegations rather than treating all defendants as interchangeable.
Check the House Ethics docket for findings after the pardon before labeling its status current.

nodes.note: Descriptive grouping from indictment, not an invented legal company name

cases.title: Cash & Gold
cases.name: Robert & Nadine Menendez

people.name: Robert Menendez
people.role: Former U.S. senator, New Jersey; former Senate Foreign Relations chair

cases.summary: A senator, his wife and businessmen formed a network that exchanged money and valuables for political influence. Robert and Nadine Menendez were separately convicted. Their case shows the full chain: a family intermediary, a foreign-backed business advantage, private benefits and official intervention.

findings.text: The June 2022 search recovered more than $480,000 in cash and more than $100,000 in gold. The scheme also included a car, mortgage support and a low-or-no-show job for Nadine.

Egypt granted Wael Hana's IS EG Halal business an exclusive certification position. The proven scheme included payments for Nadine and Menendez's attempt to pressure a USDA official to protect that business advantage.

Robert received an 11-year sentence on January 29, 2025. Nadine received 54 months on September 11, 2025. Each sentencing announcement records $922,188.10 in forfeiture; these are not two independent pots of new personal income.

money.label: Forfeiture ordered
money.legal_recipient: Forfeiture obligation imposed on defendants; not a payment to them
money.reason_excluded: Judicial remedy, not new beneficiary receipts; do not sum with seized property or double count between spouses

cases.accountability: This is an adjudicated example of a family relationship functioning as a channel between private commercial interests, foreign-government interests and a senator's official power. It supplies a documented comparison for evaluating less-resolved influence networks without assuming those other networks are criminal.

response.text: Robert Menendez denied wrongdoing and appealed. September 2026 reporting described arguments to overturn the convictions and no ruling from the bench that day. The convictions and sentences are documented events; any later appellate disposition should be checked before claiming the docket is fully current.

cases.what_is_established: Convictions, sentences, spouse/business links and the cash-and-gold evidence identified by the trial and sentencing record.
cases.what_is_not_established: That the historical seizure is new income inside FY2023–FY2026, or that every dollar of a foreign company's revenue flowed to the couple.
next_evidence: Check the Second Circuit docket for decisions after September 24, 2026 before labeling appeal status as of publication.
Extract payment-level exhibits and preserve dates so historical bribes, alleged acts and later obstruction are not collapsed into one four-year total.

cases.title: Family Contracts
cases.name: Cory Mills & Rana Al Saadi

people.name: Cory Mills
people.role: U.S. representative, Florida, during the documented contracts

people.name: Rana Al Saadi
people.role: Spouse; executive chairwoman in the Pacem businesses in the OCE record

cases.classification: Documented company awards / formal ethics referral
cases.summary: Federal ethics investigators traced nearly $1 million in munitions contracts to companies owned by Rep. Cory Mills after he entered Congress. His wife held leadership roles in the businesses. The record connects the officeholder, family, corporate ownership and federal buyers without pretending the full contract value became personal income.

findings.text: Mills disclosed 100% ownership of Pacem Defense; OCE identified his wife as executive chairwoman and ALS as the company's wholly owned subsidiary. These are the business links behind the contracts.
OCE reviewed federal purchasing records and found close to $1 million in contracts from January 2023 through its review. It counted 94 contracts awarded to Mills-owned entities from January 9, 2024.
The Board found substantial reason to believe Mills may have held or benefited from federal contracts in violation of applicable rules or law. That referral is not a final violation finding.
The House Ethics Committee reported in May 2026 that its broader investigative subcommittee had authorized more than 20 subpoenas and was continuing its work.

money.label: Federal company contracts identified by OCE
money.legal_recipient: Pacem Defense / ALS entities identified by OCE
money.personal_allocation: Ownership exposure established; retained profit and distributions not quantified

cases.accountability: The unresolved question is specific: did a member of Congress financially enjoy federal contracts through companies he owned, and how much was retained or distributed to the family? OCE identified a plausible prohibited-contracting issue, not just a social connection.

response.text: Mills denied the allegations and said he would work with the committee. His lawyer also cited dismissal of campaign-related FEC allegations; that does not establish dismissal of the separate federal-contract question.

cases.what_is_established: Named family roles, reported ownership, a subsidiary relationship, contract evidence examined by OCE and an official ethics referral.
cases.what_is_not_established: A final legal violation, the family's exact retained profit, or the assumption that nearly $1 million in corporate awards equals nearly $1 million in household cash.
next_evidence: Reconcile all 94 award records using recipient identifiers, purchase-order IDs, modifications and payment dates.
Obtain the latest company filings and divestment records; reported ownership is dated, not presumed permanent.
Read the later Ethics docket and exhibits for distribution, salary, tax or profit evidence and a final disposition.
